question.text: A PM using SWAPTIONS to hedge expected rate volatility is essentially:

answer.text: Buying optionality to enter an IRS at a predetermined rate

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines a swaption as giving the holder the right, but not the obligation, to enter into an interest-rate swap. Swaptions can be used to hedge against adverse future interest-rate movements, which is why a PM uses them to manage exposure to rate volatility rather than to express a single directional view. The Trap: Outright IRS or futures express a direction; swaptions add optionality on top of the IRS, so they are not a pure "rates will fall" or "rates will rise" forecast. They also do not eliminate all fixed-income risk — they hedge a specific rate exposure. Note: Because the holder has a right and not an obligation, the swaption is exercised only if the adverse rate move actually materialises.
